svg.title: Inheritance vs composition

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: "Favour composition over inheritance" - Design Patterns, 1994. It is still the best advice in OOP.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: - tight coupling: child knows parent's internals

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: - parent changes silently break every child

svg.text: Use it for genuine subtypes + polymorphism.

svg.text: + swap the collaborator without touching the class

svg.text: + trivially testable: pass a fake/stub logger

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: + no hidden parent state, no MRO surprises

svg.text: This is what Dependency Injection means.

svg.text: Frameworks (FastAPI, Django) are built on it.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
'Segoe UI', 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Inherit to BE something (a subtype users will treat polymorphically). Compose to USE something (a collaborator you might replace).
